newsitem.title: CHINA: China province intensifies anti-smuggling crackdown.
newsitem.headline: China province intensifies anti-smuggling crackdown.

text.p: Police in southern China's booming Guangdong province have arrested more smugglers and seized more contraband as part of an intensified crackdown on smuggling, the China Daily said on Monday.
Guangdong police busted 3,501 smuggling cases in the first nine months of 1996, a rise of 21 percent from the same period last year, the newspaper said.
Police recovered smuggled goods worth some 1.77 billion yuan ($213 million), up four percent from the year-ago period.
Guangdong, which borders thriving Hong Kong, is a hotbed for smugglers who use speedboats to ferry goods to and from the British colony.
Police arrested 149 suspects, of whom 103 were found guilty by courts, the newspaper said, adding that the number of those convicted had risen 47 percent from last year.

Guangdong authorities had formed two special anti-smuggling squads to step up patrols of porous coastal areas that were most vulnerable to smuggling, it quoted Chen Wenli, director of the provincial anti-smuggling office, as saying.

Raw materials, such as steel products, plywood, oil, paper and industrial chemicals, were the most commonly smuggled goods, accounting for more than 30 percent of the value of the confiscated contraband, Chen said.
Motor vehicles, electrical appliances and cigarettes made up another 27.8 percent of the smuggled goods seized by authorities, Chen said.
Authorities had also closed several plants making motor vehciles from smuggled parts, he said.
Chen said the coastal anti-smuggling drive had helped push smugglers out of seaports but that smuggling over land crossings from other provinces had increased as a result.
